nodes.text: Let $A\subseteq [1,n)$ be a set of integers such that $(a,b)=1$ for all distinct $a,b\in A$. Is it true that\[\sum_{a\in A}\frac{1}{n-a}\leq \sum_{p<n}\frac{1}{p}+O(1)?\]

#1210 : [Er77c,p.64] [Er80,p.112] number theory In [Er80] he claims he 'did not state [this] quite correctly' in [Er77c] . The problem in [Er77c] which Erdős is presumably referring to states that if $n<q_1<\cdots<q_k\leq m$ is the set of primes in $(n,m]$ then\[\sum \frac{1}{q_i-n}< \sum_{p<m-n}\frac{1}{p}+O(1).\]See also [460] and [950] .
